problem.statement_latex: Given finite $G$ and an oracle $f:G\to X$ constant on, and distinct between, the left cosets of unknown $H\leq G$, output generators of $H$. Complexity counts oracle queries; $n=\lceil\log_2|G|\rceil$.
problem.statement_text: Given finite $G$ and an oracle $f:G\to X$ constant on, and distinct between, the left cosets of unknown $H\leq G$, output generators of $H$. Complexity counts oracle queries; $n=\lceil\log_2|G|\rceil$.

strength.description_latex: Exponential classical queries to polynomial quantum queries.
strength.description_text: Exponential classical queries to polynomial quantum queries.

evidence.description_latex: The upper bound holds for every finite group; oracle lower bounds give an exponential worst-case classical separation.
evidence.description_text: The upper bound holds for every finite group; oracle lower bounds give an exponential worst-case classical separation.

hardware.description_latex: Polynomially many coset-state registers suffice; general joint measurements and subgroup enumeration have exponential implementation cost.
hardware.description_text: Polynomially many coset-state registers suffice; general joint measurements and subgroup enumeration have exponential implementation cost.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(n^2+\log(1/\delta))$ queries with error $\delta$ by the Ettinger--H{\o}yer--Knill subgroup-state test. An exact construction uses $O(n^4)$ queries with arbitrary one-qubit gates. General subgroup discrimination and preprocessing require exponential resources.
quantum.headline_text: $O(n^2+\log(1/\delta))$ queries with error $\delta$ by the Ettinger–Høyer–Knill subgroup-state test. An exact construction uses $O(n^4)$ queries with arbitrary one-qubit gates. General subgroup discrimination and preprocessing require exponential resources.

classical.headline_latex: Repeated birthday-collision sampling finds generators with $O(n2^{n/2})$ queries in the worst case; equal oracle values give elements of $H$. Simon-type order-two subgroups require $\Omega(2^{n/2})$ randomized queries. For finite abelian groups, subgroup-sensitive identification costs $O(\sqrt{(|G|/|H|)\log|H|}+\log|H|)$ deterministic queries.
